test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The captain exclaimed with joy that he had won the toss.

options.text: The captain said, “Hurrah! I have won the toss.”
The captain said, “Hurrah! I might win the toss.”
The captain said, “Hurrah! I may win the toss.”
The captain said, “Hurrah! I could win the toss.”

solution:
"The correct answer is **'Option 1'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "The captain exclaimed with joy that he had won the toss." is in indirect speech.
 
• In direct speech, we use quotation marks and usually, the tense gets converted to a deictic present perspective (i.e., as if the event is happening right now).
 
• Among the given options, option 1, "The captain said, “Hurrah! I have won the toss.”" correctly transforms the indirect speech into direct, maintaining the original meaning and exclamation.

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2: "The captain said, “Hurrah! I might win the toss.”" This incorrectly changes the certainty of winning the toss to a possibility.
 
• Option 3: "The captain said, “Hurrah! I may win the toss.”" This also incorrectly presents the winning as a possibility.
 
• Option 4: "The captain said, “Hurrah! I could win the toss.”" This option suggests that the captain had the ability to win the toss but doesn't confirm if he did.
